Quel'Thalas (/ˈkwɛlθəˌlɑːs/ KWEL-thuh-lahs) (Thalassian for "High Home") (sometimes spelled as Quel'thalas) is a forested area in northern Lordaeron. Known as the Land of Eternal Spring, in the northwest it is ruled by the blood elves, the descendants of the kingdom's Highborne founders. Its capital is Silvermoon City, the crown jewel of the kingdom of Quel'Thalas. In the southeast, it is ruled by the forest trolls, with their capital being the temple city Atal'Aman.
Around 6800 BDP, centuries after their exile from night elven society, Dath'Remar Sunstrider and his Highborne followers created the Sunwell, using a stolen vial of water from the Well of Eternity at a nexus of ley lines on the Isle of Quel'Danas. With the fount's power, Dath'Remar founded the kingdom of Quel'Thalas, while the land was magically bathed in an eternal springtime. Now calling themselves the high elves, they embraced the Sunwell as the very heart of their culture, since their kingdom was only made possible because of it. However, the elves earned the enmity of the forest trolls of Zul'Aman, under the Amani Empire, who wished to reclaim their ancestral lands conquered by the elves. After several long-spanning conflicts, High King Anasterian Sunstrider presided over the Troll Wars, which dealt the Amani a defeat they would never truly recover from. In its seclusion, Quel'Thalas continued to prosper with the protection of the Sunwell for millenia, repelling the Amani invasions and even the Orcish Horde during the Second War, until the kingdom's formidable defenses were bypassed by the corrupted death knight Arthas Menethil and his undead Scourge during the course of the Third War.
During the Scourge invasion of Quel'Thalas, Anasterian perished before Arthas's dark powers, the Sunwell was destroyed, and the bulk of the high elven people was slaughtered by the undead. In the wake of this devastation, Prince Kael'thas Sunstrider proclaimed the survivors reborn from the ashes of their shattered kingdom, as the blood elves. For several years, the blood elves worked tirelessly to reclaim their homeland from the lingering undead, and eventually succeeded in taking back much of their country, the capital of Silvermoon included. In a dramatic turn of events, a twisted Kael'thas returned to Quel'Thalas and attempted to summon the Burning Legion via the Sunwell. The prince's dark ambitions were not to be realized, however, and the Sunwell itself would ultimately be returned to the blood elves by the Prophet Velen. With the Sunwell restored, a bright future now lies ahead for Quel'Thalas. Following the end of the Sunstrider dynasty, Quel'Thalas is now instead led solely by its regent lord, Lor'themar Theron.
Quel'Thalas was originally introduced in Warcraft II, and its fall was first depicted during its sequel, Warcraft III. In World of Warcraft, it was initially only present in the form of an obscure, unmarked zone during the game's launch. It was later fully integrated during The Burning Crusade expansion, first with two starting locations for the Horde-aligned blood elves: Eversong Woods and the Ghostlands. A third additional level cap zone was later added during Fury of the Sunwell, the Isle of Quel'Danas. It was revisited as the primary setting for the Midnight expansion.

It was revisited as the primary setting for the ''[[World of Warcraft: Midnight|Midnight]]'' expansion.{{Ref web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=F1pkwARaVAY&t=1300s|title=BlizzCon | Opening Ceremony | World of Warcraft (21:40 - 22:40)|author=World of Warcraft|publisher=YouTube|date=2023-11-03|accessdate=2023-11-04}} {{OTOC|300|187}} ==History== {{Main|Quel'Thalas (kingdom)}} {{Main|Amani Empire}} ==Geography== [[File:WorldMap-EK Midnight Continent.jpg|thumb|upright|{{g|mn}} Quel'Thalas map.]] [[File:Quel'Thalas map.jpg|thumb|upright|{{g|bc}} Quel'Thalas map.]] *{{mn-inline}} [[Eversong Woods]] ({{level|eversong woods}}) *{{mn-inline}} [[Isle of Quel'Danas]] ({{Level|Isle of Quel'Danas}}) *{{mn-inline}} [[Zul'Aman]] ({{Level|Zul'Aman}}) ===Burning Crusade=== *{{bc-inline}} [[Eversong Woods (Burning Crusade)|Eversong Woods]] ({{level|eversong woods (burning crusade)}}) *{{bc-inline}} [[Ghostlands|The Ghostlands]] ({{Level|Ghostlands}}) *{{bc-inline}} [[Isle of Quel'Danas (Burning Crusade)|Isle of Quel'Danas]] ({{Level|Isle of Quel'Danas (Burning Crusade)}}) ===Other regions=== *{{novel-inline}} [[Thalassian Way]] *{{WC3-inline}} [[Greenwood Pass]] - Could be the [[Thalassian Pass]]. ==In World of Warcraft== ===Classic=== {{wow-section}} {{Main|Quel'Thalas/Eastern Kingdoms terrain}} [[File:Quelthalas oldworld.jpg|thumb|Location of Quel'Thalas in the Old World, swimming from Hinterlands.]] In {{g|wow}} there was a zone of the "old world" officially named '''Quel'thalas'''. It was the only glimpse of Quel'Thalas before {{g|tbc}} expansion, and was accessible in the game. See [[Northern Lordaeron]] and [[Quel'Thalas/Eastern Kingdoms terrain|this subpage]] for more information and speculation about the zone. [[Adon]] the high elf hinted that the zone was to be added in a later add-on. Prior to [[patch 4.0.3]], you could reach it by swimming along the coast from [[Tirisfal Glades]] east, or north from the [[Hinterlands]] beyond the coast of the [[Eastern Plaguelands]]. Located near the peninsula of the unnamed zone was a [[Quel'Thalas/Eastern Kingdoms terrain|tall white tower]] that was inaccessible and had a dock nearby. Following the ''[[Cataclysm]]'' expansion and the ability to fly in [[Azeroth]], invisible walls prevented conventional access to the "old" Quel'Thalas. With ''[[Battle for Azeroth]]'', the walls were removed. ===Burning Crusade=== {{bc-section}} Quel'Thalas was opened in ''[[World of Warcraft: The Burning Crusade]]'', and is split into three main regions. To the north is the [[Isle of Quel'Danas (Burning Crusade)|Isle of Quel'Danas]], home to the dragonhawks and location of the mystical [[Sunwell]]. South of Quel'Danas, across a channel of the [[North Sea]], is [[Eversong Woods (Burning Crusade)|Eversong Woods]], the blood elf starting zone and the location of their capital, [[Silvermoon City]]. To the south of Eversong, across the [[Elrendar River]], is the [[Ghostlands]]. It is here that the primary base of the Scourge in Quel'Thalas, the fortress of [[Deatholme]], is located - as is the city of [[Zul'Aman]], the capital of Quel'Thalas' long-hated enemies, the [[Amani tribe|Amani forest trolls]]. All of Quel'Thalas is bisected by a path of [[Blight (plague)|blight]] known as the [[Dead Scar]]. This was the path taken by Arthas from Lordaeron to the Sunwell in his quest to resurrect Kel'Thuzad, running from Deatholme all the way through the Ghostlands and Eversong Woods, coming to a stop midway through Quel'Danas at the gates of the [[Sunwell Plateau]]. The path is patrolled by remnants of the Scourge invasion of Quel'Thalas. All attempts by blood elf magisters to cure the blighted soil have failed, giving the blood elves more of an incentive to seek out the destiny promised them beyond the Dark Portal. Quel'Thalas is connected to the old world via the [[Thalassian Pass]] in southern Ghostlands, which goes along the main road (blocked by debris prior to Burning Crusade) into Lordaeron, in the region now called the [[Eastern Plaguelands]]. The path between Ghostlands and EPL is separated by an instance portal; the areas in which the "instance" falls under are all three regions of Quel'Thalas, both islands of the [[Azuremyst Isles]] (where the [[draenei]] start out) and all of [[Outland]]. ===Cataclysm=== {{cata-section}} While most of the rest of Azeroth has been updated in {{g|cata}}, Quel'Thalas remains as it was during the events of {{g|tbc}}, specifically, the [[Scourge]] shows no abatement as a result of Arthas' defeat; while the large [[fel crystal]]s, said to have been removed at this point in the timeline,[[What's in the Box?]] still dot the landscape in [[Eversong Woods (Burning Crusade)|Eversong Woods]] and [[Silvermoon City]]. Additionally, the [[Isle of Quel'Danas (Burning Crusade)|Isle of Quel'Danas]] should now be free of Scourge, Burning Legion, and Kael's forces; this progress can only be glimpsed during [[The Return of Quel'Delar quest chain]], in a phased version of the isle. Discounting standard city updates (the addition of new class trainers and some updated [[Blood Knight]] quest text), the conflict in [[Zul'Aman]] during [[patch 4.1.0]] marks the first major change to Quel'Thalas post-''The Burning Crusade''. ==Sources== From [http://www.findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_zdcgw/is_200512/ai_n15717842 "World of Warcraft: The Burning Crusade" in Computer Gaming World, December, 2005 by Jeff Green]: :''The blood elf starting area is [[Sunstrider Isle]] -- many thought the Scourge has destroyed most of their land, this is still a vital, healthy area -- as you can see from the screens. "We wanted a look that was the opposite of the night elf look," says Metzen, "Where the night elves live in eternal twilight, we wanted the high elves, at their best, to live in a place of eternal spring and vibrancy. Arthas has destroyed most of it, but some of it still lives on." Blizzard also wanted a different architectural vibe for the blood elves' land. "The night elves have a somewhat Nordic and Japanese architecture," says Metzen. "We wanted something more classical and magical this time."'' :''At this point Quel'Thalas is set to be composed of roughly three to five zones, including [[Eversong Forest]], the starting zone (and also the location of the blood elf capital, [[Silvermoon City]]), the [[Ghostlands]], which border the [[Eastern Plaguelands]] to the south, and the [[Sunwell Plateau]], which won't be part of the initial expansion but will be a part of a live update down the line. Blizzard is also adding a high-level instanced area, [[Zul'Aman]], home of the forest trolls, as incentive for players to take their old characters up into this new land.'' :''One key goal for Blizzard was to make sure that, for this new Horde race, there was enough variety in the zones to keep things interesting. "We wanted to mix things up more this time," says Rob Pardo, VP of game design, "We learned from Kalimdor that there was just too much of the same thing--too much desert, too much bleakness."'' :''One particularly distinctive feature of this area will be that Metzen jokingly calls the "Road o' Death," the trail that Arthas' army marched through in WarCraft III, which completely bisects the land all the way through, including Silvermoon City. "It's a constant reminder to the blood elves," says Metzen, "of just how much shit these guys have gone through."'' ==In the RPG== {{RPG-section}} In ''[[Lands of Conflict]]'', Quel'Thalas is a burned and dead land that has been dubbed [[Blackened Woods]].''[[Lands of Conflict]]'', pg. 112 ==Notes and trivia== *During the [[Second War]], [[Turalyon]] wanted to sail straight to Quel'Thalas, but Alleria assured him that would be impossible as elves would never allow human ships up their portion of the river. Instead, they disembarked near [[Stratholme]].''[[Tides of Darkness]]'', chapter 12 **In modern ''[[World of Warcraft]]'' geography, [[Thondroril River]] is near [[Stratholme]] and it continues it continues to the closed [[northern Lordaeron]]. As such, it could be speculated it continues into Quel'Thalas itself. **In ''[[Warcraft III]]'' geography, however, there was a river going from the [[Darrowmere Lake]] up to Quel'Thalas, dividing [[Zul'Aman]][[:File:LordaeronWC3.JPG]] (which in the RPG books was named [[Greenrush River]]). *During the [[Fourth War]], the [[Horde]] sent a massive force to march on [[Arathi Highlands|Arathi]] and take [[Stromgarde Keep]] in order to use it as a launching point for [[Gilneas]].[http://wow.zamimg.com/uploads/screenshots/normal/673330.jpg BlizzCon 2017 - ''Gameplay and Systems'' panel] The [[Alliance]] in return sent their armies to protect the Stromic lands and continue their conquest of the Eastern Kingdoms, by cutting off the north, especially [[Silvermoon City]].[https://warcraft.blizzplanet.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/DivXSnap-2017-11-07-20-41-33-751-1920x1080.jpg BlizzCon 2017 - ''Gameplay and Systems'' panel] *The demonym for a citizen of Quel'Thalas is Thalassian, sometimes Quel'Thalassian.''[[Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos]]'' [[Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos Game Manual|manual]] *It is hinted that the [[Azj'Aqir|aqiri empire]] stretched as far as the lands that would much later be known as Quel'Thalas.''[[Blood of the Highborne]]'': "[[Liadrin]] was reminded of the tales she had heard of the long-forgotten aqir, the sentient insect race whose ancestors once inhabited this very land but were driven out by the trolls millennia ago." *Snowing was possible in the southern border of the kingdom,''[[In the Shadow of the Sun]]''[[The Dead Rise as Quel'thalas Falls (WC2 Orc)]] though it is possible that it is only possible after the fall of Quel'Thalas. *The map published in the ''Warcraft II'' manual shows several regions including Khaz Modan, Quel'Thalas, and Lordaeron, each sharing the same font size. Azeroth is shown with a larger font size.[[:File:Second War Map.jpg]] *The name in the ''Warcraft II'' manuals was written as "Quel'thalas".[[Warcraft II: Tides of Darkness manual]][[Warcraft II: Beyond the Dark Portal manual]] This is also the name of the [[Quel'Thalas/Eastern Kingdoms terrain|unused zone]] in the northern part of the Eastern Kingdoms in WoW. *According to a non-canon RPG source, Quel'Thalas is implied to be a separate continent.''[[Alliance Player's Guide]]'', pg. 178: "Lordaeron (and the surrounding regions such as Quel'Thalas)..." *It has not been confirmed what the region was called before the high elves settled it and named it Quel'Thalas. ==Speculation== {{Speculation}} ===Ban'dinoriel=== The power of the [[Sunwell]] - manifesting in a massive arcane shield known as [[Ban'dinoriel]] - was once used as a great defensive measure to protect [[Silvermoon City]]. It was considered to be impenetrable. During the Second War, it was enough to ward off an onslaught of enslaved [[red dragon]]s, and during the Third War it halted the Scourge army's advance until the invaders, using knowledge gleaned from a traitor, were able to dispel it. With the Sunwell restored, it is unclear if it still holds these considerable powers of protection.
